report.releaseDate: Nov 2026 (Delaware Lottery unaudited monthly tables for the Oct-26 accounting period, posted ~10–19 Nov 2026; trade coverage 27 Nov 2026)
report.currency: USD (market reports in USD; tables in $ millions unless stated)
report.verdict: October 2026 confirms Delaware as a small, state-run, single-vendor market whose growth now comes almost entirely from online casino: combined sports + iGaming wagers hit a record $396.3m (+16.6% YoY) and iGaming NGR rose 18.8% to $13.05m, while sports handle fell 8.4% and retail casino win slipped 1.4% to $38.4m. The state's take is rising faster than the market (sports state share +23.6%) because the Lottery keeps 50–90% of net proceeds under a revenue-share, not a tax. For an operator the market remains closed — entry is only via the Lottery's vendor contract (RSI/BetRivers, base term to ~2028) or B2B content supply — and the 2024 multi-operator bill is dead.
summary: **Record combined wagering, driven by online casino.** Delaware Lottery tables show sports handle of $26.01m plus iGaming bets of $370.24m = $396.25m in October 2026, +16.6% YoY (Oct-25: $339.8m) and +6.0% on September; iGaming bets grew 18.9% while sports sales fell 8.4%.

**iGaming is the growth engine.** NGR (bets less promo deductions less player winnings) was $13.05m, +18.8% YoY, +1.6% MoM: online slots $9.97m (+28.0%), online tables $3.03m (-2.5%), poker $38.6k (-52.3%). FYTD (Jul–Oct FY27) NGR is $52.29m (+31.4%); FY26 full year was $135.93m (+59% per secondary arithmetic on Lottery tables, implying FY25 ≈ $85.5m).

**Sports: fewer bets, fatter hold, more for the state.** Tickets fell 17.5% to 1.22m and handle 8.4% to $26.01m, but hold rose to 17.6% (13.9% a year ago), lifting gross win 16.0% to $4.57m, net proceeds (after $1.58m vendor fees) 18.9% to $2.82m and the state share 23.6% to $1.80m. Secondary coverage ranks it the sixth-best handle month since full-scale launch on 5 Jun 2018.

**Retail casinos are flat-to-down.** CDC Gaming, citing the Lottery, puts October casino win at $38.4m (-1.4%): VLTs $35.1m (-1.0%), table games $3.0m (-6.8%). Delaware Park +1.3% to $16.8m was the only grower; Bally's Dover -3.7% to $12.4m; Harrington -3.3% to $9.2m. Prior months: Jul -3.7%, Aug -2.6%, Sep -5.4%.

**Total market ≈ $54.3m in October; online casino ≈ 24%.** Summing retail casino win ($38.4m), iGaming NGR ($13.05m) and sports net proceeds ($2.82m) gives ~$54.3m: retail ~71%, online casino ~24%, sports ~5%. FYTD ≈ $210.5m. The Lottery does not split sports between BetRivers mobile and retail books, so true online penetration is understated.

**Structure: a state-conducted lottery monopoly.** All casino gaming, iGaming and sports wagering are Lottery games under 29 Del. C. ch. 48; the State Lottery Office (Dept. of Finance) is operator-regulator and the Division of Gaming Enforcement handles licensing investigations/enforcement (the tables are explicitly 'before operating expenses for Lottery and Division of Gaming Enforcement'). Three racinos are 'video lottery agents'; one contracted vendor (Rush Street Interactive) runs all online product.

**No open licensing route.** RSI won the Lottery's 2023 procurement (two bidders) for a five-year contract with annual renewal options and launched BetRivers-branded casino sites for all three racinos plus the single BetRivers sportsbook app on 27 Dec 2023 (replacing the prior 888 platform). There is no application window; suppliers reach players via the RSI platform (Hacksaw Gaming launched slots through BetRivers in Nov 2026).

**The 'tax' is a revenue share — and it is steep.** Sports: net proceeds (sales − prizes − vendor fees) are split 50% State / ~10% purses / ~40% commission at casino sportsbooks and ~90% State at Lottery retailers (verified from the October table arithmetic); blended state share was 64.0% of net proceeds, 39.5% of gross win, 6.9% of handle. Video lottery: ~37.5% General Fund / ~44% agent commission / ~10.7% purses / ~7.8% vendor (Lottery website). iGaming and table-game splits are not disclosed monthly [unverified this cycle].

**Vendor economics are large.** Sports vendor fees were $1.58m in October (34.6% of gross win; 6.1% of handle; +15.3% YoY) and $4.89m FYTD (36.2% of gross win). In FY26 vendors took $13.37m of $37.11m gross win — about the same as the state's $13.11m.

**Operator concentration.** Delaware Park holds 54.0% of sports handle (incl. allocated mobile) and 46.1% of iGaming NGR; Harrington 19.9% / 30.2%; Bally's Dover 10.8% / 23.7% but is the fastest grower (iGaming NGR +30.3% YoY, FYTD +60.8%; sports net proceeds +35.4%).

**Parlay-card retailers punch above their weight.** Lottery retailers took 15.2% of handle ($3.96m, +11.8%) but produced 34.8% of net proceeds ($0.98m, +44.3%) and 49.0% of the state share ($0.88m) because the state keeps ~90% of retailer proceeds.

**Promo intensity is minimal.** iGaming promo/adjustment deductions were $2.45m, 0.66% of bets (0.62% a year ago; 0.71% FY26) — an order of magnitude below multi-operator states, a direct consequence of single-vendor exclusivity.

**The acquisition funnel is slowing.** New iGaming registrations fell to 3,963 (-36.2% YoY; -25.1% MoM) and 18,474 FYTD (-21.9%) versus a 5,245 monthly average in FY26; growth is now spend-per-player and retention, consistent with year three of a monopoly platform in a ~1m-population state.

**Hold rates are stable in iGaming.** Slots NGR/bets 4.42% (4.53% Oct-25; 4.51% FY26); tables 2.10% (2.23%; 2.02%). Slots are 76.4% of NGR, up from 70.9% a year ago — the mix is drifting toward higher-margin slots.

**Legislation to open the market is stalled.** HB 365 (152nd General Assembly, Reps Cooke/Bush, Apr 2024) would have allowed each racino two mobile sportsbook skins (six total) at a $500k five-year licence, 18% of adjusted gross sports receipts to the General Fund and 1.5% to purses, codifying the Internet Sports Lottery Legislative Working Group's recommendation. The Lottery and Finance Secretary opposed it (revenue loss, contract risk, federal excise exposure) and it died without a Senate vote at the Jun 2024 adjournment; no successor had been enacted as of Nov 2026 [2025–26 session activity not verified].

**Federal excise is a hidden structural feature.** Because wagers are state-conducted lottery products, the 0.25% federal excise on sports handle does not apply; a private-operator model would trigger it — one of the state's stated objections to opening the market.

**Payments, RG and advertising are low-friction and lightly specified.** Standard US regulated rails (ACH/online banking, debit, e-wallets, cage) apply; no Delaware-specific advertising code; Lottery/DGE self-exclusion and a 21+ age floor are the core safeguards [method mix, limits and RG statistics not published; unverified this cycle]. College wagering on Delaware schools is restricted per secondary sources.

**Read-through for B2Tech.** Delaware is not enterable as a B2C operator before the RSI base term ends (~late 2028), and even then only as the single Lottery vendor. The TAM is small (~$37m sports gross win and ~$136m iGaming NGR in FY26; ~$160–170m iGaming NGR FY27 est.). Realistic plays: (i) B2B content/platform supply to RSI, (ii) position for the 2028 re-procurement, (iii) support a racino-backed multi-skin bill. Model any entry at a 50%+ state take on sports unless the statute changes.

**Data caveats.** Monthly tables are unaudited; retail casino figures are secondary and the prior-year October base ($38.9m implied vs $35.1m reported last year) suggests an accounting-period mismatch; Gaming Intelligence's combined-revenue figure ($15.7m) is slightly below our arithmetic from the Lottery tables ($15.86m = $2.82m sports net proceeds + $13.05m iGaming NGR).

segments.name: Sports betting (racino sportsbooks, Lottery parlay-card retailers, BetRivers mobile)
segments.headline: Handle -8.4% to $26.0m but a 17.6% hold lifted net proceeds 18.9% and the state's cut 23.6%; retailers' parlay cards now deliver half the state share.
narrative: Delaware's sports lottery took $26.01m in wagers in the four-week accounting period 28 Sep–25 Oct 2026, down 8.4% from $28.40m a year earlier and up 3.7% on September ($25.09m). Ticket count fell harder, -17.5% to 1.22m, so the average ticket rose to $21.25 from $19.14. The Lottery's table pools BetRivers mobile wagers with each racino's retail book and shows Lottery retailers (parlay cards) separately; it does not disclose the mobile share, which is the single biggest gap in the dataset for anyone modelling online penetration.

Hold did the work. Prizes paid were $21.45m, leaving gross win of $4.57m (+16.0% YoY) and a 17.6% hold against 13.9% in October 2025 and 17.3% in September. FYTD hold is 15.5% versus 12.5% in the prior-year period; FY26 full-year was 14.7% on $252.46m handle (gross win $37.11m). A parlay-heavy mix — retailer parlay cards plus mobile parlays — is structurally high-hold, but two consecutive months above 17% is unusual even for Delaware and should not be annualised; a reversion to 13–15% would cut gross win by roughly a fifth at constant handle (estimate).

After vendor fees of $1.58m (34.6% of gross win; 6.1% of handle; +15.3% YoY), net proceeds were $2.82m (+18.9%). Vendor fees have run at 36.2% of gross win FYTD against 34.6% a year earlier, so the Lottery's contracted vendors (RSI/Kambi for mobile and Scientific Games for the retail books, per secondary sources) are capturing more than a third of gross win before any public distribution — in FY26 $13.37m, roughly equal to the state's own $13.11m.

The distribution mechanics are visible in the table: for the three racino sportsbooks, net proceeds split 50% State / ~10% horse-racing purses / ~40% commission (Delaware Park: $1.18m net → $590k State, $113k purses, $477k commission), while Lottery retailers hand ~90% to the State ($980k net → $883k) with purses ~10% and retailer commission apparently funded outside net proceeds. Blended, the state took $1.80m, 64.0% of net proceeds (61.5% a year ago), 39.5% of gross win and 6.9% of handle. FY26 state share was $13.11m, 5.2% of handle.

By channel, Delaware Park (the largest retail book and, by Lottery allocation, most of the mobile volume) took $14.05m (54.0% of handle; -15.4% YoY) yet grew net proceeds 11.9% to $1.18m; Harrington $5.19m (-9.5%; net -10.5% to $399k); Bally's Dover $2.82m (+12.3%; net +35.4% to $259k); Lottery retailers $3.96m (+11.8%; net +44.3% to $980k). Retailers are 15.2% of handle but 34.8% of net proceeds and 49.0% of the state share — per dollar wagered, the parlay-card network is the most fiscally productive channel in the state, which explains the Lottery's attachment to it.

FYTD (Jul–Oct FY27): handle $87.38m (+3.0%), tickets 3.80m (-10.6%), gross win $13.52m (+27.5%), net proceeds $8.20m (+26.8%), state share $4.96m (+27.0%). Flat handle with rising hold and a rising state take is the signature of a maturing single-app market in which bettors migrate to parlays and pricing is thinner than in the multi-operator markets next door (NJ, PA, MD). Secondary sources note calendar-2025 handle of $253.3m and revenue of $20.7m (8.2% hold on their definition).

Commercially, Delaware's sports pool is ~$37m of gross win a year, of which ~$13m reaches the General Fund and ~$13m goes to vendors; no single entrant could materially change the TAM, and the state's objection to opening the market is that it would "shift State revenues to sports wagering companies and also trigger federal excise taxes" (Finance Secretary, via Delaware Business Times). The commercially relevant prize is therefore the vendor position itself, not a licence.

segments.name: Online casino (iGaming: internet video lottery, table games, poker)
segments.headline: NGR +18.8% to $13.05m on record bets of $370m; slots carry the growth (+28%) while registrations fall 36% — the market is deepening, not widening.
narrative: iGaming bets reached $370.24m in October (+18.9% YoY; +6.2% MoM), a record, with online slots (the Lottery's 'internet video lottery') at $225.49m (+31.0%) and online table games at $144.75m (+3.9%). NGR — bets less promo/adjustment deductions less player winnings — was $13.05m (+18.8% YoY; +1.6% MoM): slots $9.97m (76.4% of NGR; +28.0%), tables $3.03m (23.3%; -2.5%) and poker $38.6k (-52.3%). Slots were 74.0% of FY26 NGR, so the mix continues to drift toward the higher-margin product.

Hold rates are stable: slots 4.42% of bets (4.53% a year ago; 4.51% FY26) and tables 2.10% (2.23%; 2.02% FY26). Promo deductions were $2.45m, 0.66% of bets (0.62% a year ago; 0.71% FY26). That is a fraction of bonusing in multi-operator states and is the clearest financial fingerprint of a single-vendor market: there is no competitor to bid up acquisition cost, so the economics accrue to the vendor, the racinos and the state rather than to players.

FYTD NGR is $52.29m (+31.4%) on bets of $1,425m (+25.3%). FY26 (Jul-25–Jun-26) NGR was $135.93m on bets of $3,947m — +59% YoY by secondary arithmetic on the Lottery's tables (implying FY25 ≈ $85.5m). October annualises to ~$157m. Growth is decelerating from the step-change that followed RSI's replacement of the 888 platform on 27 Dec 2023, but remains comfortably double-digit; we estimate FY27 NGR of $160–170m (Jul–Oct actual $52.3m plus Nov–Jun at +15–20% on FY26's ~$96m for those months).

The player funnel is softening. New registrations were 3,963 in October (-36.2% YoY; -25.1% MoM) and 18,474 FYTD (-21.9%), against a 5,245 monthly average in FY26. Revenue growth is therefore coming from spend-per-player and retention rather than acquisition — the expected profile in year three of a monopoly platform serving a state of roughly one million residents, and an early warning that the online growth rate will converge toward retail trends within two to three years absent new product or a competitive catalyst.

By skin — each racino's BetRivers-powered site on the same platform, game library and sportsbook — Delaware Park took $6.02m (46.1% share; +17.8%), Harrington $3.94m (30.2%; +12.4%) and Bally's Dover $3.09m (23.7%; +30.3%, the fastest grower, FYTD +60.8%). Differentiation is limited to brand and loyalty cross-sell to the physical racino. Hacksaw Gaming's November 2026 slot launch via BetRivers shows that the content pipeline into Delaware runs through RSI's aggregation, which is the only realistic B2B route for a supplier.

The Lottery's monthly table reports NGR before vendor fees and before Lottery/DGE operating expenses; the statutory split of internet gaming proceeds between the State, purses and agents, and RSI's vendor fee, are not disclosed monthly [unverified this cycle] and appear only in the Lottery's annual financial statements. Commercially, Delaware iGaming is a ~$150–170m NGR pool with 0.7% promo intensity and no second platform — excellent unit economics for the incumbent vendor and inaccessible to everyone else until re-procurement.

segments.name: Retail casinos (video lottery & table games) and lottery
segments.headline: Three racinos generated $38.4m of win (-1.4%); VLTs -1.0%, tables -6.8%; only Delaware Park grew — the land-based estate is mature and purse-dependent.
narrative: The three racinos generated $38.4m of casino win in October 2026 (-1.4% YoY) according to CDC Gaming citing the Lottery: VLTs $35.1m (-1.0%) and table games $3.0m (-6.8%). Delaware Park was the only property to grow (+1.3% to $16.8m; VLT +4.8% to $15.3m; tables -24.9% to $1.5m); Bally's Dover fell 3.7% to $12.4m (VLT -3.0% to $11.5m; tables -11.3% to $0.89m); Harrington fell 3.3% to $9.2m (VLT -7.5% to $8.5m; tables +122% to $0.69m off a depressed base).

The trend is gentle erosion: July $33.4m (-3.7%), August $43.8m (-2.6%), September $34.4m (-5.4%), October $38.4m (-1.4%) — roughly $150m FYTD. Table games are the weak spot (-19.7% Jul, -11.3% Sep, -6.8% Oct). One reconciliation flag: last year's October release reported $35.1m, whereas this year's -1.4% implies a ~$38.9m base, which points to a different accounting-period length; the primary video-lottery table could not be fetched this cycle, so the YoY is indicative rather than verified.

Combined with online, the Delaware gaming market produced ~$54.3m in October (retail casino win $38.4m, iGaming NGR $13.05m, sports net proceeds $2.82m): retail ~71%, online casino ~24%, sports ~5%. iGaming NGR is now equivalent to 34% of retail casino win. With retail flat-to-down and online growing ~20%, the online share rises about one to three points a year depending on the retail base used (estimate) — slow by European standards, but the direction is unambiguous and the racinos capture it through their skins.

Economics for the racinos follow the Lottery's published distribution: ~44% of video lottery revenue is paid to the three tracks as commission, ~37.5% goes to the State General Fund, ~10.7% to horse-racing purses and ~7.8% to leasing, servicing and central-system monitoring. Games must by law return 87–95% of wagers annually (above 95% with the Director's approval), and the state floor has more than 6,200 VLTs. Table-game distribution percentages were not verified in this cycle. Traditional lottery (draw, instant, Keno) sales are not in the monthly gaming tables and are n/a here.

Implication: the retail estate is mature and intertwined with horse-racing subsidies (purses take ~10% of sports and VLT proceeds), which is why the three incumbents and the horsemen are influential in any legislative change and why HB 365 was structured around racino-tethered skins. An entrant's only retail route is acquiring a racino (Bally's Dover belongs to the listed Bally's Corporation; the other two are privately held).

segments.name: Licensing, tax & revenue distribution
segments.headline: No licences to apply for: a state-conducted lottery with three racino agents and one online vendor; the state keeps 50–90% of sports net proceeds and ~37.5% of VLT win.
narrative: All casino gaming, iGaming and sports wagering in Delaware are conducted as lottery games by the Delaware State Lottery Office (Department of Finance) under Title 29, Chapter 48 of the Delaware Code; the Division of Gaming Enforcement (Department of Safety and Homeland Security) conducts licensing investigations and enforcement — the Lottery's tables are explicitly reported 'before operating expenses for Lottery and Division of Gaming Enforcement'. There are no commercial casino or sportsbook licences in the usual sense: the three racetracks are 'video lottery agents' and the online operator is a contracted Lottery vendor.

Online, the Lottery ran a procurement in 2023 for a single iGaming and internet-sports vendor; two companies applied and Rush Street Interactive won a five-year contract with annual renewal options (Delaware Business Times), launching BetRivers-powered casino sites for all three racinos and the single BetRivers sportsbook app on 27 Dec 2023. The base term therefore runs to late 2028, with the Lottery able to extend annually. No application window exists for additional operators; suppliers reach the market through RSI's platform.

Sports distribution is verifiable from the October table: net proceeds = sales − prizes − vendor fees; at the racino sportsbooks the split is 50% State / ~10% purses / ~40% commission, and at Lottery retailers ~90% State / ~10% purses. Blended, the state took 64.0% of net proceeds in October. Secondary sources describe this as a '50% tax', but it is a revenue share inside a state-conducted lottery — which also means the 0.25% federal excise on sports wagers does not apply, a point the Finance Secretary used against HB 365.

Video lottery distribution (Lottery website): ~37.5% General Fund, ~44% agent commission, ~10.7% purses, ~7.8% vendor/central system. Table games: state share not verified in this cycle [unverified]. iGaming: the statutory split between State, purses and agents and RSI's vendor fee are not disclosed in the monthly tables [unverified]. Secondary sources also cite an annual fee of roughly $4.5m shared by the three casinos pro rata to video-lottery market share, not tied solely to sports [secondary, unverified].

Reform attempts: HB 365 (152nd General Assembly, Reps Franklin Cooke and William Bush, April 2024) would have let each racino partner with up to two mobile sportsbooks (six skins), with a $500,000 five-year licence fee, 18% of monthly adjusted gross sports receipts to the General Fund and 1.5% to purses, codifying the Internet Sports Lottery Legislative Working Group's recommendation that multiple operators generate more volume. The Lottery and Finance Secretary opposed it on revenue, contract-risk and federal-excise grounds; it died without a Senate vote at the 30 Jun 2024 adjournment. No successor measure had been enacted as of November 2026 (2025–26 session activity not verified in this cycle).

For an operator, Delaware's effective state take on sports is the highest in the US (50% of net proceeds at casinos, ~90% at retailers, versus 18% of adjusted gross receipts proposed under HB 365), and iGaming economics are set by contract rather than statute. The practical entry options are (i) bid in the next vendor procurement (~2028), (ii) B2B supply (content, trading, platform components) to RSI, or (iii) support a racino-backed multi-skin bill — recognising that the Lottery's institutional mandate to maximise state revenue, and the absence of federal excise under the current model, weigh against change.

segments.name: Payments, responsible gambling, advertising & political direction
segments.headline: Low-friction US payment rails and minimal bonusing (0.66% of bets); no Delaware-specific ad code; the political centre of gravity is the Lottery's revenue mandate, with the 2028 vendor renewal the only hard catalyst.
narrative: Payments run through the standard US regulated rails for a state-licensed online casino and sportsbook (ACH/online banking, debit cards, e-wallets, cash at the racino cage); there is no mobile-money analogue and the Lottery publishes no deposit-method mix. BetRivers' Delaware-specific method list and limits were not verified in this cycle [n/a]. Nothing in the data suggests payment friction constrains growth — iGaming bets of $370m a month are 14x sports handle, and slots turnover grew 31% YoY.

Responsible gambling is administered by the Lottery with the DGE: self-exclusion, a 21+ age floor for casino, iGaming and sports products, and the state problem-gambling helpline are the core safeguards [programme details and statistics not published monthly; unverified this cycle]. The measurable proxy is promotional intensity: iGaming promo/adjustment deductions were $2.45m, 0.66% of bets, versus 0.71% in FY26 — bonus-driven stimulation is minimal by design of the single-vendor model.

Advertising faces no Delaware-specific statutory code comparable to Ontario or the UK; under the single-vendor structure marketing is a Lottery/RSI decision rather than a competitive arms race, and the state's exposure to multi-operator advertising saturation is nil. College wagering on Delaware-based schools and college player props is restricted per secondary sources [unverified].

Political direction favours the status quo. The Lottery's stated job is to maximise state revenue, and under the current model it keeps 64% of sports net proceeds and avoids federal excise. Three forces could shift it: the 2028 vendor renewal; the racinos' interest in multiple skins (HB 365 was built around them); and competitive leakage to NJ/PA/MD apps and to federally regulated prediction markets, which affiliate sites already market to Delaware users (Kalshi, Polymarket and similar). No enforcement actions were reported in the period; the notable commercial event was Hacksaw Gaming's content launch via BetRivers.

Lead indicators to monitor: the FY2028 budget cycle (Jan–Jun 2027) for any Lottery revenue re-forecast or re-filed multi-operator bill; monthly iGaming registrations as the saturation gauge (currently -36% YoY); sports hold normalisation toward 13–15%, which would cut the state's sports take by roughly a fifth at constant handle (estimate); and any Lottery statement on extending or re-tendering the RSI contract ahead of the late-2028 base-term expiry.

highlights.text: Online casino is in structural growth: NGR +18.8% YoY in October, +31.4% FYTD, with slots +28% and hold stable at ~4.4% — a ~$160–170m FY27 NGR pool (est.) with only one platform serving it.
The B2B door is open: Hacksaw Gaming's November 2026 launch via BetRivers shows content and platform suppliers can reach Delaware players through RSI's aggregation without any state licence.

Monopoly economics: promo deductions are just 0.66% of iGaming bets and sports hold is running 15–18%, so revenue per dollar wagered is far higher than in open multi-operator states — attractive for whoever holds the vendor contract.

A defined re-procurement window: RSI's five-year base term from Aug 2023 ends in late 2028; the Lottery's 2023 tender drew only two bidders, so a credible challenger faces thin competition for the only B2C route into the state.

The state's own Working Group has already recommended up to six mobile skins tethered to the racinos; a re-filed HB 365-style bill (18% of adjusted gross receipts, $500k five-year licence) would be a step-change in operator economics versus today's 50% revenue share.

Retail parlay cards are a durable niche: Lottery retailers took 15% of handle but delivered 49% of the state's sports share, a product format that keeps the retail network politically protected and commercially relevant.

lowlights.text: The market is closed: no licence application exists, all online product runs through one Lottery vendor to ~2028, and HB 365 died without a Senate vote in June 2024 with the Lottery and Finance Secretary opposed.

Tiny addressable pool: FY26 sports gross win was $37.1m (state share $13.1m, vendor fees $13.4m) and October handle fell 8.4% with tickets -17.5%; even a 100% share would be immaterial to a multi-state operator.

Punitive state take: 50% of sports net proceeds at casino books and ~90% at retailers (64% blended in October), the steepest effective rate in the US; iGaming and table-game splits are undisclosed monthly, adding modelling risk.

iGaming acquisition is decelerating: new registrations fell 36% YoY to 3,963 (18,474 FYTD, -22%), so growth now depends on spend-per-player — the online growth rate will converge toward retail trends within two to three years absent a catalyst.

Retail is eroding: casino win -1.4% in October after -5.4% in September and -3.7% in July; table games -6.8% to -19.7% across the quarter; two of three racinos declined — cannibalisation by the skins is visible.

Sports hold of 17.6% (vs 13.9% a year ago) flatters the state's +23.6% take; normalisation to 13–15% would cut gross win by roughly a fifth at constant handle (estimate), exposing the underlying handle decline.

Governance and data opacity: monthly tables are unaudited, mobile vs retail sports volume is not disclosed, retail casino figures could only be sourced second-hand this cycle with an unexplained prior-year base mismatch ($35.1m vs ~$38.9m), and legislative activity in the 2025–26 session could not be verified.

Substitution risk from outside the state framework: multi-operator apps in NJ/PA/MD and federally regulated prediction markets are marketed to Delaware users, eroding the case for — and the value of — single-vendor exclusivity.

forecast.intro: A market has no guidance, so the bridge compares the FY2026 base (Jul-25–Jun-26) with the FY2027 run-rate implied by Jul–Oct 2026. iGaming is the driver: FYTD NGR +31.4% against FY26's +59%, so growth is halving but still double-digit; sports gross win is +27.5% FYTD on flat handle (+3.0%) purely through hold; retail casino win is tracking roughly -3% (secondary). Regulatory moving parts are few: RSI's exclusive contract (base term to ~late 2028), no multi-operator bill since HB 365 died in June 2024, no tax or distribution change proposed, and the FY2028 budget cycle (Jan–Jun 2027) as the next formal point at which the Lottery's revenue forecast and any expansion bill would surface.

forecast.view: **Market:** we expect FY27 iGaming NGR of $160–170m (+18–25%) with growth decelerating through 2027 as registrations fall and the player base saturates; sports handle flat to -5% with hold reverting toward 14–15%, leaving net proceeds up low-double-digits for the fiscal year but flat-to-down by mid-2027 on tougher comparatives; retail casino win -2% to -4% as the skins cannibalise VLT play. **Total gaming revenue** (retail win + iGaming NGR + sports net proceeds) should therefore grow low-to-mid single digits to roughly $650–670m in FY27 (estimate), with online casino's share rising to ~26–27%. **State take** rises faster than the market because the online and parlay channels carry the highest public shares. **Rules:** no change in 2027; the realistic catalyst is the 2028 vendor renewal, and we put the probability of a multi-operator mobile sports bill passing before that renewal at well under one in three — the Lottery's revenue mandate, the federal-excise argument and the racinos' comfortable skin economics all favour continuity. **Swing factors:** a re-filed racino-backed skins bill with purse protections; a Lottery decision to re-tender rather than extend RSI; evidence of leakage to prediction markets or neighbouring states large enough to change the Finance Department's arithmetic; and any national federal action on prediction markets. **For B2Tech:** treat Delaware as a B2B content/platform opportunity now and a 2028 vendor-tender option later; a B2C entry case does not exist under current law, and any model should carry a 50%+ state share on sports and undisclosed iGaming economics until the statute changes.
watch: Monthly iGaming registrations (3,963 in Oct, -36% YoY) — the saturation gauge; sustained sub-4,000 months would confirm convergence toward retail growth rates.
Sports hold reverting from 17–18% toward 13–15% — the main risk to the state's +24% take and to the Lottery's defence of the single-app model.
FY2028 Governor's budget (Jan 2027) and the 2027 legislative session for any re-filed multi-operator mobile bill (HB 365 template: six skins, $500k/5-yr, 18% of AGR, 1.5% purses).
Lottery signalling on the RSI contract (base term to ~late 2028): annual extension versus re-tender, and whether the next RFP contemplates more than one vendor.
Retail casino win trend (Jul–Oct -1% to -5%) and table-game weakness; a second year of decline strengthens the racinos' case for additional online skins.
Reconciliation of the retail casino accounting periods (Oct-25 base $35.1m vs ~$38.9m implied) once the Lottery's video-lottery table is accessible.
Prediction-market and cross-border leakage: any Delaware DGE/Lottery statement on Kalshi-type event contracts, and NJ/PA/MD geolocation-blocking data if published.

Sports lottery and iGaming figures (Oct-26, Oct-25, Sep-26, FYTD and FY26) were read directly from the Delaware Lottery's unaudited monthly tables and all percentages are our arithmetic on those tables. Retail casino (VLT/table) figures are secondary (CDC Gaming citing the Lottery) because the Lottery's video-lottery table could not be fetched; the implied Oct-25 base (~$38.9m) does not reconcile with last year's reported $35.1m, so the -1.4% YoY is indicative. Gaming Intelligence's combined-revenue figure ($15.7m) is slightly below our $15.86m from the tables.
